conventions: In a construct chain whose nomen rectum carries an article, count the ASV's written *the*s and let the count decide, rule 29; a segmented article on a toponym is read on exactly the terms of one on a common noun. One *the* with the rectum rendered anarthrously goes to the present article and the construct noun keeps only its own word — the way to Bashan (3.1), the king of Bashan (3.1, 3.3), half the hill country of Gilead (3.12), the rest of Gilead, the half tribe of Manasseh, the region of Argob (3.13), the slopes of Pisgah (3.17), the top of Pisgah (3.27). Two written *the*s give each morpheme the one standing before its own word — the hand of the two kings of the Amorites (3.8), the remnant of the Rephaim (3.11), the border of the Geshurites (3.14), the middle of the valley (3.16), the sea of the Arabah (3.17). No *the* at all leaves the article `unrepresented` — all Gilead, all Bashan (3.10, 3.13), king of Bashan (3.11), and the bare toponyms of 3.15, 3.16 and 3.25. The same toponym appears all three ways in this chapter, so a supplied *the* on the construct is licensed only where no article morpheme stands or where a second English *the* is written.

Where such a chain is also a directional or locative accusative, the preposition rule 33 supplies for the accusative and the *the* rule 29 gives the rectum's article both stand in the phrase, and the construct's unit is discontinuous around the article rather than absorbing it: `רֹאשׁ הַפִּסְגָּה` → *unto* … *top* with the article's *the* between them (3.27), and `אַשְׁדֹּת הַפִּסְגָּה` → *the slopes of Pisgah* on the same terms with no preposition supplied (3.17). Do not fold the *the* into the construct noun's unit to make it contiguous; the fronting is forced by the anarthrous rendering of the rectum, not by the phrase's left edge.
report: Read all 29 verses end to end against the 60-lemma candidate table, plus the four `added` units the table cannot see and both large-source-unit candidates (3.5 unit 10, 3.21 unit 36). No cross-verse split remains; verdict no-change.

Construct-chain articles were the chapter's one real risk and are now uniform. I checked all 88 Td tokens individually: every `aligned` one stands before its own word or is a rectum article fronted because the ASV renders the rectum anarthrously, and every `unrepresented` one either has no *the* written for the phrase or has been outbid by a demonstrative (six times in the temporal phrase, five in the demonstrative phrases), a suffix (3.24 thy strong hand) or a numeral (3.21 these two kings). Verses 12, 13, 17 and 27 were corrected during the verse pass; 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 11, 14 and 16 already agreed. The same toponym appears with one written *the*, with two, and with none in this chapter, so the count decides and never the position.

The remaining table groups are context, not splits. The preposition-plus-construct fusion rendered *beyond* is identical in 3.8, 3.20 and 3.25, carrying a copula only where the ASV writes one (adjunct in 3.20, predicate in 3.8 and 3.25). A present relative takes the English relative in 3.8, 3.12 and 3.25, while a clause with no relative morpheme leaves the supplied one `added` in 3.9 and 3.16 — that pair is the `added`-blind case, checked by hand and consistent. Supplied *thereof* is `added` in both 3.16 and 3.17 for the same anarthrous noun. The waw takes *even* and the following limit preposition takes *unto* in 3.16 twice and in 3.17, which is rule 16's own stated limit rather than a competing convention.

The two participle-article buckets look like a split and are not: in 3.21 the article is `unrepresented` because the ASV recasts the participle as the main verb (*Thine eyes have seen*) and writes neither relative nor determiner for it, while in 3.22 it takes *that* because the ASV writes one. Rule 41's closing sentence governs both.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. The Td (33), R (10) and To (5) blocks are the documented convention difference on function morphemes. DEU.3.24 the 1cs suffix of the divine title is rule 57's lexicalized suffix, and the ASV writes no possessive anywhere in the title. DEU.3.26 the adverb is a reasoned rule-22 call — the ASV spends two English words (*no more*) on three morphemes, the negative, the verb of repetition and the adverb — and the verse note names the competing reading. No accepted edge was changed to improve an aggregate.

Four defensible ties were left standing rather than traded for a score, each already naming its alternative under rule 8: the head of *over against* in 3.29 (the corpus precedent nearest to hand, *round about* headed on *round*, would head it on *over*); *as unto you* in 3.20 read as one compound rendering rather than as rule 25 distribution of the earlier dative; *no more* in 3.26; and the fronted measure predicate carrying the copula in 3.11.

No promotion. The nearest thing to a gap is the supplied volitive frame on a predicate adjective in 3.26 (*Let it suffice thee*), which rule 20's construction-supplied copula and rule 17's volitive-frame sentence already reach between them. It occurs once, and the packet carries no corpus precedent for it, so a rule resting on it would be paid for by every chapter after this one.
